name: Nebuchadnezzar
charge: Pride: is not this great Babylon, that I have built?
summary: Warned by Daniel's interpretation of the tree dream to break off his sins by righteousness and his iniquities by showing mercy to the poor, the king walked on his palace roof twelve months later and took the credit for the empire. While the word was in his mouth a voice fell from heaven.
offense: Nebuchadnezzar received a dream warning that his greatness would be cut down until he knew that the Most High rules in the kingdom of men. Daniel interpreted it and counseled him to break off his sins by righteousness and his iniquities by showing mercy to the poor (Daniel 4:19-27). The warning offered instruction before the sentence fell. Twelve months later the king walked in his palace and boasted of Babylon as the work of his own might for the honor of his majesty. He treated entrusted dominion as an achievement belonging wholly to himself. The words were still in his mouth when the heavenly answer declared that his kingdom had departed (Daniel 4:28-32).
judgment: He was driven from men, ate grass as oxen, and was wet with the dew of heaven until the appointed times passed. His dependence was exposed beneath the grandeur in which he had gloried. At the end he lifted his eyes to heaven, his understanding returned, and he blessed the Most High. His counselors sought him again, his kingdom was restored, and he confessed that the King of heaven can abase those who walk in pride (Daniel 4:33-37). The restored king's testimony gave God the honor his former boast had claimed for himself.

verses.text: Wherefore, O king, let my counsel be acceptable unto thee, and break off thy sins by righteousness, and thine iniquities by shewing mercy to the poor; if it may be a lengthening of thy tranquillity.
All this came upon the king Nebuchadnezzar.
At the end of twelve months he walked in the palace of the kingdom of Babylon.
The king spake, and said, Is not this great Babylon, that I have built for the house of the kingdom by the might of my power, and for the honour of my majesty?
While the word was in the king’s mouth, there fell a voice from heaven, saying, O king Nebuchadnezzar, to thee it is spoken; The kingdom is departed from thee.

And they shall drive thee from men, and thy dwelling shall be with the beasts of the field: they shall make thee to eat grass as oxen, and seven times shall pass over thee, until thou know that the most High ruleth in the kingdom of men, and giveth it to whomsoever he will.

The same hour was the thing fulfilled upon Nebuchadnezzar: and he was driven from men, and did eat grass as oxen, and his body was wet with the dew of heaven, till his hairs were grown like eagles’ feathers, and his nails like birds’ claws.

And at the end of the days I Nebuchadnezzar lifted up mine eyes unto heaven, and mine understanding returned unto me, and I blessed the most High, and I praised and honoured him that liveth for ever, whose dominion is an everlasting dominion, and his kingdom is from generation to generation:

And all the inhabitants of the earth are reputed as nothing: and he doeth according to his will in the army of heaven, and among the inhabitants of the earth: and none can stay his hand, or say unto him, What doest thou?

At the same time my reason returned unto me; and for the glory of my kingdom, mine honour and brightness returned unto me; and my counsellors and my lords sought unto me; and I was established in my kingdom, and excellent majesty was added unto me.
Now I Nebuchadnezzar praise and extol and honour the King of heaven, all whose works are truth, and his ways judgment: and those that walk in pride he is able to abase.
O thou king, the most high God gave Nebuchadnezzar thy father a kingdom, and majesty, and glory, and honour:

And for the majesty that he gave him, all people, nations, and languages, trembled and feared before him: whom he would he slew; and whom he would he kept alive; and whom he would he set up; and whom he would he put down.
But when his heart was lifted up, and his mind hardened in pride, he was deposed from his kingly throne, and they took his glory from him:

And he was driven from the sons of men; and his heart was made like the beasts, and his dwelling was with the wild asses: they fed him with grass like oxen, and his body was wet with the dew of heaven; till he knew that the most high God ruled in the kingdom of men, and that he appointeth over it whomsoever he will.

Now if ye be ready that at what time ye hear the sound of the cornet, flute, harp, sackbut, psaltery, and dulcimer, and all kinds of musick, ye fall down and worship the image which I have made; well: but if ye worship not, ye shall be cast the same hour into the midst of a burning fiery furnace; and who is that God that shall deliver you out of my hands?
And now have I given all these lands into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon, my servant; and the beasts of the field have I given him also to serve him.
And all nations shall serve him, and his son, and his son’s son, until the very time of his land come: and then many nations and great kings shall serve themselves of him.
The beginning of pride is when one departeth from God, and his heart is turned away from his Maker.
For pride is the beginning of sin, and he that hath it shall pour out abomination: and therefore the Lord brought upon them strange calamities, and overthrew them utterly.

entries.commentary: Nebuchadnezzar proclaimed to all people, nations, and languages the signs and wonders the high God worked toward him, whose kingdom is everlasting, then told how a dream made him afraid and he decreed to bring in all the wise men of Babylon to interpret it. Remember from the day before that he had already brought in all his wise men once and they could not recall or interpret his dream; when the captain went out to slay the wise men he came upon Daniel, who was granted favour, consulted the Most High, and was given the vision.

The magicians, astrologers, Chaldeans, and soothsayers could not make known the interpretation, but at last Daniel came in, named Belteshazzar after the king's god, in whom is the spirit of the holy gods. Daniel was named after one of the king's gods. It is the same thing as Hadassah, whose name was changed to Esther; this is not new for us.

Nebuchadnezzar saw a great tree reaching to heaven, feeding and sheltering all flesh, then a watcher and a holy one came down and commanded it hewn down, its stump left bound with iron and brass, its heart changed to a beast's, till seven times pass over him. The matter is by the decree of the watchers, to the intent that the living may know that the Most High ruleth in the kingdom of men and giveth it to whomsoever he will and setteth over it the basest of men. That is what we see today, the basest of men ruling the earth. -

Daniel, astonished for an hour, told the king the dream was for his enemies: the tree is the king himself, grown strong to the ends of the earth. The decree of the Most High is that he shall be driven from men to dwell with the beasts and eat grass as oxen, wet with the dew of heaven, till seven times pass and he knows the Most High ruleth; the stump left means his kingdom is kept for him once he knows the heavens do rule. Daniel counselled him to break off his sins by righteousness and his iniquities by shewing mercy to the poor, that his tranquillity might be lengthened. You need to walk in righteousness and show mercy to the poor.

Twelve months later, walking in his palace, the king boasted, is not this great Babylon that I have built by my might for the honour of my majesty. He was very proud and boastful. While the word was in his mouth a voice from heaven pronounced the kingdom departed, and the same hour he was driven from men, ate grass as oxen, his hairs grown like eagles' feathers and his nails like birds' claws.

At the end of the days Nebuchadnezzar lifted his eyes to heaven, his understanding returned, and he blessed and honoured the Most High, whose dominion is everlasting and before whom all the inhabitants of the earth are reputed as nothing. None can stay his hand or say unto him, what doest thou. When the Most High declares a thing shall come to pass, it comes to pass. -

His reason and the glory of his kingdom returned, and he praised and extolled the King of heaven, whose works are truth and ways judgment, and who is able to abase those that walk in pride. We already understood that the Most High can bring one up and set another down, but the heathen had to learn it by being jacked up, literally turned to crawl like a bird with the heart of a beast; as soon as his understanding returned he praised the one true living God. -

Belshazzar the king made a great feast to a thousand of his lords and, while tasting the wine, commanded the golden and silver vessels his father Nebuchadnezzar had taken from the temple in Jerusalem be brought so he, his princes, wives, and concubines might drink in them. This is Belshazzar the king, not Belteshazzar, who is Daniel. They drank and praised the gods of gold, silver, brass, iron, wood, and stone. -

In the same hour fingers of a man's hand wrote on the plaster of the wall, and the king's countenance changed, his knees smote together, so terrified that the joints of his loins were loosed. Picture him sitting back drinking with his lords, wives, and concubines, having a good time, and then a hand starts writing on the wall; he was terrified out of everything. He cried aloud for the astrologers, Chaldeans, and soothsayers, offering scarlet, a gold chain, and to be third ruler in the kingdom to whoever could read it, but none of his wise men could read the writing or interpret it, and he was greatly troubled.

The queen came into the banquet house and told the king of the man Daniel, in whom is the spirit of the holy gods, whom Nebuchadnezzar his father had made master of the magicians because an excellent spirit, knowledge, and understanding were found in him. Daniel was brought in, and the king offered him scarlet, a gold chain, and the third rulership if he could read the writing and make known the interpretation.

Daniel told the king to keep his gifts and rewards, then recounted how the Most High gave Nebuchadnezzar his kingdom and greatness, and how, when his heart was lifted up in pride, he was deposed and driven to dwell with the wild asses until he knew the Most High ruleth in the kingdom of men. Belshazzar had not humbled his heart though he knew all this, but lifted himself against the Lord of heaven, drank from the temple vessels, and praised gods of silver, gold, brass, iron, wood, and stone that see not nor hear, while the God in whose hand his breath is he did not glorify. -

Daniel read the writing: MENE, MENE, TEKEL, UPHARSIN. MENE, God has numbered the kingdom and finished it; TEKEL, the king is weighed in the balances and found wanting; PERES, the kingdom is divided and given to the Medes and Persians.

Belshazzar clothed Daniel with scarlet, put a chain about his neck, and proclaimed him third ruler, but that same night Belshazzar the king of the Chaldeans was slain and Darius the Median took the kingdom, being about threescore and two years old. Immediately after the interpretation the kingdom was translated from Belshazzar to the Medes and Persians.

Nebuchadnezzar made an image of gold, threescore cubits high and six cubits broad, and set it up in the plain of Dura, then gathered the princes, governors, captains, judges, treasurers, counsellors, sheriffs, and rulers to its dedication. We have seen things like this before. When they build a monument or a new federal building they hold a dedication and a ribbon-cutting ceremony. This is very similar.

A herald cried that when the people heard the cornet, flute, harp, sackbut, psaltery, dulcimer, and all kinds of music they were to fall down and worship the golden image. We see the same thing today when they play the national anthem at ball games and ceremonies. You are supposed to take your hat off and put your hand over your heart. That is a form of worshipping the image of the eagle today.

Whoever did not fall down and worship would the same hour be cast into the midst of the burning fiery furnace, so when the music sounded all the people, nations, and languages fell down and worshipped the golden image.

Certain Chaldeans came near and accused the Jews, telling the king that Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, whom he had set over the affairs of the province, did not regard him, serve his gods, nor worship the golden image. The reason we did not bow was according to the law. -

In his rage Nebuchadnezzar brought the three men and demanded whether they would fall down and worship, threatening the furnace and asking, who is that God that shall deliver you out of my hands. He is talking tough, talking big, challenging our God when he asks who is going to deliver you out of his hands.

The three answered that they were not careful to answer him in this matter: their God whom they serve is able to deliver them from the burning fiery furnace and out of the king's hand. But if not, be it known unto thee, O king, that they would not serve his gods nor worship the golden image. This is exactly what was read in [Exodus 20](/bible/exodus/20).

Full of fury, Nebuchadnezzar commanded the furnace heated seven times more than usual and had his mighty men bind the three in their coats and garments and cast them in. The furnace was so hot that the flame slew the men who carried Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego up to it. For more of this history the Song of the Three Holy Children can be read; for the sake of time it was only referenced here.

The three men fell down bound into the furnace, but Nebuchadnezzar rose up astonished and said he saw four men loose, walking in the midst of the fire, unhurt, and the form of the fourth was like the Son of God.

Nebuchadnezzar called them servants of the Most High God to come forth, and the fire had no power on their bodies: not a hair singed, their coats unchanged, nor the smell of fire on them. It was as if they had never fallen into the fire; not even the smell of smoke was on these brothers.

Nebuchadnezzar blessed the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, who sent his angel to deliver the servants that trusted in him and would not serve nor worship any god except their own God. He understood at that time that we had our own God. Why do people not understand that today. He decreed that any people, nation, or language that spake amiss against their God would be cut in pieces, because there is no other God that can deliver after this sort, and he promoted the three in the province of Babylon. When the nations get jacked up they come to know who has the real, true, living God; other heathen rulers came to the same acknowledgement, such as Antiochus and Naaman the Syrian. -

The Most High tells Jeremiah to make bonds and yokes, put them on his neck, and send them to the kings of Edom, Moab, Ammon, Tyrus, and Zidon by their messengers to Zedekiah. The Most High made the earth, man, and beast by His power and outstretched arm and gives it to whom it seems meet to Him; He has now given all these lands and the beasts of the field into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar His servant. All the nations shall serve him, his son, and his son's son until the time of his land comes, when many nations and great kings shall serve themselves of him; the Most High uses people, He used Nebuchadnezzar, Cyrus, and Pharaoh alike.

The nation and kingdom that will not serve Nebuchadnezzar and will not put its neck under the yoke of Babylon the Most High will punish with the sword, the famine, and the pestilence until they are consumed. Therefore they must not hearken to their prophets, diviners, dreamers, enchanters, and sorcerers who say they shall not serve the king of Babylon, for they prophesy a lie. The nations that bring their neck under the yoke and serve him He will let remain in their own land to till it and dwell there; this is the Most High saying that whatever we are commanded to do, even the other nations are told to serve Babylon or answer to Him.

Jeremiah speaks the same words to Zedekiah, telling him to bring his neck under the yoke of the king of Babylon and serve him and live, rather than die by the sword, the famine, and the pestilence. He is not to hearken to the prophets who say he shall not serve Babylon, for they prophesy a lie in the Most High's name that will drive the people out to perish along with the prophets themselves.

Jeremiah warns the priests and all the people not to listen to the prophets who claim the vessels of the Lord's house will shortly be brought back from Babylon, for they prophesy a lie; they should serve the king of Babylon and live. If they were true prophets they would make intercession that the remaining vessels not go to Babylon, but instead the pillars, the sea, the bases, and the residue of the vessels shall be carried to Babylon and remain there until the day the Most High visits them and restores them to this place. The whole warning is that Babylon is one the Most High will use to take over everything, and the people had better listen and serve him, because all these prophecies were meant to happen and they did happen. --- Topics: [Clean and Unclean Meats](/encyclopedia/clean-and-unclean-meats) · [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

A haughty heart leads to destruction.
Curses and punishments are due to those who neglect the poor or withhold from him his needs.
The boastful shall not stand in God's sight.
